fit.sheet: Valvo AC128 data sheet (Valvo Halbleiterdioden und Transistoren, 8.63, pages 123-129)
fit.figure: page 126 IB against IE at UCB = 0 (mean, to 10 mA); page 128 B bei -UCE = 1 V (10 to 500 mA); page 127 -UBE against IE at UCB = 0 (mean, both ranges); page 124 table (rbb', Cb'c, f1); page 129 ICBO at 25 °C; page 125 output curves (VAF)
fit.method: Gummel-Poon (scripts/fit_models.py). IS, NF, BF, ISE, NE, IKF, NKF and RE by least squares on the gain and VBE points together, taken as at VCE = 1 V (the UCB = 0 curves sit at VCE ≈ VBE, 0.1-0.47 V: the sheet gives VBE's change with VCE as 0.4 mV/V, and the Early effect moves the gain 2-3 %, less than the two gain figures disagree at 10 mA: 86 at UCB = 0, 82 at 1 V). RB 25 Ω, the sheet's rbb'. VAF 29 V from the IB = 1 mA output line (the 2 mA line gives 43 V; the curves above it are heated). BR set so ICBO at 10 V is the mean 3.7 µA, NR = NF: there is no VCE(sat) curve, and IS alone would leak far more (an alloy transistor's reverse gain is high). CJC from Cb'c 100 pF at 5 V with the default grading; no emitter capacitance given. TF from f1 1.5 MHz at 10 mA. EG 0.67 (germanium): with XTI 3 the card's VBE moves −2.2 mV/K against the sheet's −2.3. Fitted points are matched within 4.9 % (gain) and 3.2 mV (VBE to 10 mA; 13 mV over the whole curve). The curves are raster scans, read by .claude/skills/fit-model/worked/ac128/trace.py
fit.note: One AC128 for every unit (D-170): the sheet's gain spread is 55 to 175, so a circuit sets its transistors' measured hFE and leakage (D-130). The ElectroSmash cards AC128-B85 and AC128-B120 are replaced; old circuits migrate to this card with those gains.
